explanations.a: This is an incorrect option. This combination forms bronze, not brass.
explanations.b: This is the correct option. Brass is defined as an alloy of copper and zinc, giving good strength and corrosion resistance.
explanations.c: This is an incorrect option. This forms cupronickel, commonly used in coins and marine applications.
explanations.d: This is an incorrect option. Copper–iron alloys are not classified as brass and are rarely used due to poor mutual solubility.

questions.question: 2. Extraction of Titanium is done through

explanations.a: This is an incorrect option. Pidgeon’s process is used for the extraction of magnesium, not titanium.
explanations.b: This is an incorrect option. Bayer’s process is used for refining bauxite to alumina in aluminium extraction.
explanations.c: This is the correct option. In the Kroll process, titanium is extracted by reducing TiCl<sub>4</sub> with magnesium in an inert atmosphere.
explanations.d: This is an incorrect option because titanium is extracted by the Kroll process.

questions.question: 3. Annealing improves which property of the alloy system

explanations.a: This is an incorrect option. Annealing generally reduces hardness by relieving internal stresses.
explanations.b: This is an incorrect option. Annealing usually decreases strength due to softening of the alloy.
explanations.c: This is the correct option. Annealing increases ductility by allowing recrystallization and grain growth.
explanations.d: This is an incorrect option. While toughness may improve, annealing is primarily known for improving ductility.

questions.question: 4. The third most abundant element in Earth’s crust

explanations.a: This is an incorrect option. Titanium is relatively abundant but ranks around 9<sup>th</sup> in the Earth’s crust, not third.
explanations.b: This is the correct option. Aluminium is the third most abundant element in the Earth’s crust after oxygen and silicon.
explanations.c: This is an incorrect option. Copper is a trace element in the Earth’s crust and far less abundant than aluminium.
explanations.d: This is an incorrect option. Nickel is more abundant in the Earth’s core but is not among the top three elements in the crust.

questions.question: 5. Famous heat treatment used in Al-4.5% Cu alloy is

explanations.a: This is an incorrect option. Water quenching is only an intermediate step to retain a supersaturated solid solution, not the primary heat treatment.
explanations.b: This is the correct option. Aging (precipitation hardening) is the famous heat treatment used in Al–Cu alloys to increase strength by forming fine precipitates.
explanations.c: This is an incorrect option. Normalizing is mainly used for steels and is not applicable to aluminium alloys.
explanations.d: This is an incorrect option. Surface hardening methods are generally used for steels and not for Al–Cu alloys.
